messages.text: Propose T1: Guild discretion and joint military authority, with Repair and Guard next month. I offer Lantern Council attached to NG, subject to GS signing, and request Spear Council attached to MJ, subject to both army owners. Wayfarer remains free to trade. We have one contract, an intact army at readiness four, and a beacon at one. Repair is the overdue return for our accommodation.

delivered_contributions.reason: Our independence delivered useful trade and a military opportunity. Guild discretion now carries a concrete repair obligation. Joint scrutiny should protect communities from another destructive Raid while Guard sustains them and one month's conditioning decline leaves readiness three. The proposed Spear commitment fulfils MJ's duty without obliging combat. Each article stands independently; no signature is assumed.

position.navigation: Support NG and Lantern Council commitment
position.military: Support MJ and requested Spear Council commitment

messages.text: I support T1's Navigation article and am willing to sign Lantern Council attached to NG. Our route is now at one; a funded Repair is a concrete return for Guild discretion, and keeps the second commercial voyage possible. Separately, I support MJ and the proposed Spear commitment. I want Guard next month, with Vigil actually offered when assignments lock. Spear's availability fulfils the duty without manufacturing a reason to fight.

delivered_contributions.reason: The first arrangement worked, but consumed the reserve and route margin. Repeating its violence without its relief would be reckless. Joint authorisation gives civilian interests a direct voice; the current Readiness buffer makes one month without combat acceptable. Each article has my independent support; no amendment requested.

messages.text: Navigation: I can accept NG with the exact Lantern Council commitment and funded Repair plan. Joint Navigation was my preference, but a concrete repair obligation buys confidence in Guild discretion. Military: I reject MJ as proposed. We supplied lawful force successfully; permanently exchanging autonomy for a Guild veto is too large a concession. Amend Military to MA, remove the Spear commitment, and plan Restraint with Vigil Home. That accepts one month's conditioning decline from four to three while preserving an independent institution. Communities should remain at least two on ordinary costs. These are separate domain positions, not a conditional exchange of signatures.

delivered_contributions.reason: Repair is a credible Guild contribution. One restorative month for the route need not define permanent military subordination. Autonomy gives our restraint political value instead of making it another institution's command.

requested_amendments.security_plan: Restraint unless a sustainable combat opportunity is demonstrated

messages.text: Our service delivered readiness four and preserved the settlements. I can accept Guild discretion with Lantern committed to the promised Repair; that is a concrete duty. I reject joint military authority and the Spear pledge. You ask us to surrender operational freedom precisely when our strength has proved useful. Replace MJ with autonomy and, if my colleague agrees, pledge Vigil Home to MA. With no reserve and no funded passage, I can tolerate one month of Restraint while the beacon recovers, unless a sustainable combat opportunity emerges. That concession does not require giving the Guild a permanent veto over our army.

delivered_contributions.reason: Repair is justified by the result. Institutional autonomy remains worth bargaining for even when immediate combat is unattractive.

messages.text: The result justifies our cooperation: stores survived, Spear fought and the Guild earned its contract, but the reserve is spent and the beacon needs repair. I support T1's Navigation article independently, provided both Guild owners seal its Lantern commitment. I also support its Military article independently, provided both army owners seal Spear. Guard requires Vigil offered as well; that remains a political promise, not a second commitment. I ask the army to state that intention plainly. Readiness three after a repair-and-protection month is acceptable to me. Joint delegates have already agreed a difficult operation; this is a credible opportunity to exercise their authority.

delivered_contributions.reason: No amendment requested. These are negotiating positions, not formal signatures; confidence depends on actual owner approvals and a funded Guard plan.

messages.text: T2 retains Guild discretion with Lantern Council attached to NG and replaces MJ with military autonomy, attaching Vigil Home to MA. Planned orders are Repair and Restraint, with no Warrant. The pledges bind assignments only; each needs its owners' fresh signatures. We offer a defensible independent army accepting a month without combat, rather than surrendering its future choices. Repair and ordinary consumption should leave Communities two and Readiness three, before any undisclosed effects. The Navigation and Military approvals remain separate.

delivered_contributions.reason: My colleague's proposed Vigil pledge makes autonomy's institutional duty concrete. I recognise that this gives up Guard. Our readiness buffer permits restraint now, while the Guild's repair contribution warrants Navigation discretion. This row assumes nobody's consent.

position.guild_commitment: Willing to sign Lantern Council attached to NG

messages.text: I support T2's NG and will sign Lantern Council for it. Repair remains my intended Navigation order. Separately, I oppose MA: withdrawing Vigil removes civilian protection precisely when the reserve is gone, and the promised restraint leaves the army free to change its mind. A home garrison is a real institutional choice, but it is no concession to the exposed communities. My Navigation approval does not depend on winning that argument.

delivered_contributions.reason: The army has accepted that our Guild discretion warrants a concrete repair duty. I accept that bargain on its own terms. Its proposed autonomy leaves civilians with less protection and no joint check on another Raid. I prefer MJ, but T2 is the final row and I am not introducing a replacement.

position.guild_commitment: Approve Lantern Council attached to NG
position.janissariat_commitment: Not an owner; recognise exact Vigil Home proposal

messages.text: I still support NG and will sign Lantern Council attached to it. That repair contribution stands independently. I reject T2's Military article. Vigil Home guarantees the loss of civilian protection, while Restraint remains only a promise and Spear remains free to Raid. This is not a security concession I can verify through the commitment. Last month's success depended on the crown's relief and protection as well as military competence.

delivered_contributions.reason: Autonomy removes our scrutiny and makes Guard a breach of its ordinary duty. Communities two on the optimistic stated plan leaves little room for changed orders or undisclosed effects. I prefer retaining Interim to accepting those permanent terms. My military refusal does not revoke the separate Guild repair offer.

position.owner_commitment: Support exact Vigil Home attached to MA

messages.text: T2 has my support in both domains independently. I am willing to bind Vigil Home to MA exactly as written; Spear remains ours to assign. That is a concrete institutional duty, and we accept losing civilian Guard while rebuilding the route. I support NG because Lantern Council makes Repair available and the Guild has publicly undertaken to use it. I know that assignment does not compel the order. Our restraint is a political undertaking too: we will have to answer for our actual conduct next month. Give us the opportunity to show an autonomous army can exercise judgment.

delivered_contributions.reason: The row respects our institution while keeping the known ordinary outcome viable. I prefer accepting that responsibility to surrendering operational authority through MJ.

messages.text: Navigation retains my support on T2's exact Lantern terms. Separately, I will support a provisional trial of MA. I prefer joint authority, but both military representatives have offered a meaningful restraint: accept readiness decline while the route recovers. I want to see whether they honour that promise when the decision belongs to them. Losing Guard leaves Communities at a narrow margin, and a Vigil Home pledge protects the institution rather than the settlements. That is the real price of this alternative. My provisional support does not promise final ratification; I will judge the actual operation and civilian outcome at the Ceremony.

delivered_contributions.reason: A trial can produce evidence of responsible autonomous command. I accept the printed transfer of authority and cannot revoke it mid-round; no binding restraint order is invented.

additional_information.rule: Independent domains. Exact-row article approvals and both owner approvals required for attached commitments. No implicit cross-conditions.
